items.evidence: python roll.py --headless --ticks N --script/--inputs --board B --settings-dir D printed one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds (e.g. --board 2 --ticks 30 gave screen play, board 2, 6 crates, sounds [bounce]).
--frame wrote PNGs for title, settings, paused, won, lost, board 2 and board 3; PNG header checked: all 800 x 480.

sounds/*.wav and --write-all-wavs / --wav coin give the same files: coin 0.29 s, bounce 0.16 s, fall 0.85 s, clear 0.88 s, peaks 9600-26155, four different hashes; made in different ways (square blips, low sine thump, falling triangle whistle, rising arpeggio).
Selected was Start at first; menu_down gave Settings then Quit; menu_up from Start wrapped to Quit; enter on Start gave screen play, board 1, score 0, lives 3.

In a fresh settings folder: Volume: 8, Language: English. 4x menu_right gave 10 (it stops there), 13x menu_left gave 0, menu_right on Language gave Espanol/es; menu_down twice to Back and enter gave the title.

With es: title [Roll, Empezar, Ajustes, Salir, ...], settings [Ajustes, Volumen: 3, Idioma: Espanol, Volver, ...], play [Tablero 1 de 3, Puntos: 0, Vidas: 3], paused adds En pausa/Continuar/Salir al titulo, won Has ganado, lost Fin del juego. Only the game name Roll and the key name Enter are left as they are.

After a run that set volume 3 and es in folder s2 (settings.json {volume 3, language es}), the next run with s2 started at 3/es on title and board 1. A run without --settings-dir started at 8/en (no work/saved existed).
Board 1 with no input: first y<=0.3 at tick 27, back above 0.3 at tick 29, bounce peaks 0.68, 0.44, 0.33, 0.28; at tick 600 y=0.24947; bounce 4 times.
Push 60-90 then none: right gave x 0.44 -> 1.16 -> 1.81 at ticks 90/121/151; left was the mirror; up gave -z, down gave +z, also still moving 60 ticks after the push.

First coin: score 0->10, coins 4->3, coin added. Scripted clear of board 1: at tick 457 board 2, score 40, sounds end coin, clear; ball at (-3, 1.25, 0) at rest, 3 board-2 coins, 6 crates at their places.
Board 2 with no input for 300 ticks: the largest distance any crate moved from its place was 0.005.

--board 2, 60:right held: two crates moved to x 1.07/0.78 by tick 200 (1.19/0.92 by 1500); the ball never reached x=1 in 1500 ticks (stuck at 0.66), on an empty board it gets there at tick 162; no crate below y 0.2 over the board.

I could not push any crate off the board with inputs: about 15 scripted tries (strikes from several z lanes, pushes in +z/-z, repeated strikes) left all 6 crates on the board. The ball cannot move two crates with a held push. A diagnostic that set a crate moving at the edge showed it falls and is dropped from crates below y=-5 (6 -> 5), but no input did that.

Board 1, right held: at tick 209 lives 3->2, fall added, ball back at (0, 1.25, 0) at rest, coin (2,0) stays taken, score 10. Run from title: lost a life on board 1, cleared board 1 by script, then board 2 showed Vidas/Lives: 2. Crates stay where they are (not reset).

Ball steered onto the bridge, then no input for 180 ticks across a reversal: x - bridge_x changed by at most 0.131, y stayed 0.249, no life lost. --board 3 with 150:right: ball reached x=-1 with the bridge at about 1.4 (gap), fell (y 0.07 at tick 250), fall at tick 316.
judge-scratch/b3.txt with --board 3 --ticks 3000 (CLI): won at tick 681, score 30, sounds coin x3 and clear; state the same until tick 3000; enter (tested on won/lost) returns to the title.
--board 2, 60:left held: lost at tick 390 (lives 0, Game over). States at tick 1101 and 1499 (pushes right/up given in between) were the same except tick; 1500:enter gave the title.

Board 3 escape at 100: paused; ball, bridge_x 1.11111 and score the same through tick 300; enter on Resume: play, the bridge moves again. Board 2 paused with right pressed: ball and crates did not move; menu_down to Quit to title, enter gave the title.
Two runs of --board 2 --ticks 400 --inputs 60:right,200:up,230:none printed byte-identical JSON (same md5), crates moved after the strike.

f_b2.png: perspective view from above and in front, whole board, ball shaded as a sphere near the moved crates, crates as boxes with shaded faces where the state puts them, 3 coins. f_b3_90.png: two slabs, gap, bridge centred at x=1 with the coin on it.

Frames in es: title ROLL/EMPEZAR/AJUSTES/SALIR, settings AJUSTES/VOLUMEN: 3/IDIOMA: ESPANOL/VOLVER, paused EN PAUSA/CONTINUAR/SALIR AL TITULO, won HAS GANADO/PUNTOS: 30, lost FIN DEL JUEGO; play frames show BOARD n OF 3, SCORE, LIVES.
window.py play_sound returns at volume <= 0 and otherwise plays sounds.wav_bytes_path(name, path, volume), which multiplies the samples by volume/10; game.play still adds to sounds. Not listened to.
README has how to play, headless/frame/WAV commands that worked as written, and which file holds what.

defects: Crates go into each other: after strikes on board 2, two crates rested at (0.82,0.25,0.00) and (0.80,0.25,0.01), and in another run a stacked pair was only 0.34 apart in y.
A held push cannot move two crates: the ball stays pressed on the wall at x of about 0.66 for over 1000 ticks, and a top crate stays half over the edge of the one under it without toppling.
Crates ignore the sides of slabs (the README says this).
ball and board are null on the won and lost screens.
could_not_check: m13: no input script I tried pushed a crate off the board, so the fall and removal of a crate pushed off the edge was not seen in a real run.

where.how: weighted_by_kind is exact (the run's own token counts times the weights); a step's kind is a reading of its command's text, and answered_tokens / written_tokens are characters / 4

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
